audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[].side gave 'Skill' for Level 6 and First item and 'Skill' again for 2+ items, while the packet chart and content win[] both read Talon for rows 0-5 and Azir for row 6. Three rows rendered two different answers.
audit.why: packet.levelChart = Talon x6 then Azir; content win[0..6] identical; win rate 47.45% over 746 games. The full layer was the outlier.
audit.corrected: phases[4].side and phases[5].side -> Talon, phases[6].side -> Azir, with all three whys rewritten in the same proposal so the row and the sentence agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level 6 spike was described as 'Noxian Diplomacy adds true-damage execute right at level 6' in whys[4], spikes[1].text and content.mid. Noxian Diplomacy is his Q, available at level 1, and nothing in his kit is a true-damage execute. His level 6 is Shadow Assault.
audit.why: Enemy kit R Shadow Assault, 100/80/60s, 550 range: 'disperses a ring of blades and becomes Invisible while gaining additional Move Speed. When Talon emerges from Invisibility, the blades converge on his location.' Enemy kit Q Noxian Diplomacy, 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, 575 range, leaps if the target is outside melee range and refunds health and cooldown on a kill.
audit.corrected: whys[4], spikes[1].text and content.mid now describe Shadow Assault: 100s at rank 1, invisibility, bonus move speed, blades converging when he reappears. No execute, no true damage claimed anywhere.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer repeatedly names a 'Rake-Cutthroat combo' (whys[0], spikes[0].text, content.early) and 'wall-jump Rake' (wants.foe[0]). Cutthroat is not one of Talon's abilities; the wall vault is Assassin's Path and the leap is Noxian Diplomacy. The passive, Blade's End, is never mentioned at all even though the three-Wound bleed is most of his kill pressure.
audit.why: Enemy kit P Blade's End: 'Talon's spells Wound champions, stacking up to 3 times. When Talon attacks a champion with 3 stacks of Wound, they bleed for heavy damage over time.' E Assassin's Path: 725 range, no cooldown of its own, 'puts the used terrain on a long cooldown'. Riot's ability list for Talon is Blade's End / Noxian Diplomacy / Rake / Assassin's Path / Shadow Assault.
audit.corrected: Every 'Cutthroat' reference replaced with the real ability, the Blade's End three-Wound bleed added to enemyWin, tradeBad and spikes[0].text, and the free-recast-but-terrain-locked nature of Assassin's Path stated in breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[1].d.

audit.whatIsWrong: packet.defects: no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere. breakdown.cooldowns held no digit, and dosFull[2].d offered a 'fifteen-second invitation' off Rake, which is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7.
audit.why: Defect catalogue item 3; enemy kit W Rake 9/8.5/8/7.5/7, Q 8/7.5/7/6.5/6, R 100/80/60.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, report[9].t and loading now key everything to Rake's 9s and the Q's 8s; the fifteen-second line is gone.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string pasted verbatim under a roaming title and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string pasted verbatim under a pinging title. dontsFull[1].d quoted 'nineteen seconds' for Shifting Sands; rank 1 is 22s.
audit.why: Defect catalogue items 2 and 6; ownerKit E 22/20.5/19/17.5/16.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to answer their titles; Shifting Sands quoted at 22s.

edits.before: Talon is built to murder exactly this matchup — his Rake-into-Cutthroat combo lets him vault walls from brush, burst your low base HP down in an instant, and vanish with the same skill before your soldiers can punish him, so from level 1 through level 6 you're playing purely defensive, warding constantly, and praying you don't get caught out even once since a single mistake often means a dead Azir.

edits.before: Even at level 6 his Ultimate adds true-damage execute onto an already lethal combo, so the assassination threat doesn't meaningfully ease up until you've got real HP and a defensive item to survive the initial burst — this is one of the roughest lanes in the whole mid pool and you're mostly surviving rather than contesting.

notes: This matchup carried a fabricated ability: the content layer used 'Cutthroat', which Talon does not have, in whys[0], spikes[0].text and content.early, and attributed a true-damage execute ultimate to Noxian Diplomacy (his Q) in whys[4], spikes[1].text and content.mid. All six are corrected against Riot's text. Level chart: the full layer read Skill on rows 4-6 while the packet and content both read Talon/Talon/Azir; moved the full layer to them with whys rewritten. phases[].rating left untouched.
